subject: Quality Assurance & Testing
title: Path Coverage
description: A short lesson to help you apply Path Coverage.

hook.text: A function has 3 if-statements. That's 8 possible paths through the code. Testing all 8 is path coverage.

buildup.text: Path coverage requires testing every unique route through the code—every combination of branches taken.

discovery.text: It catches bugs that only appear when specific sequences of decisions combine in unexpected ways.

twist.text: Loops make path coverage explosive. A loop running 0, 1, or N times multiplies paths dramatically.

climax.text: Full path coverage is usually impractical. Teams target critical paths and high-risk decision combinations.

punchline.text: Every path through the code. Ideal in theory, selective in practice.

quiz.question: Why is full path coverage usually impractical?
